sentences.text: The genus Herugavialis contains only one known species, Herugavialis cairensis.
Unlike all living crocodilians, this animal lacked a specific bone process within its lacrimal gland.
Scientists identify the species by unique traits such as its telescoped eye sockets.
Researchers transferred this species into the new genus Herugavialis during a study published in 2026.
The fossils were unearthed in Egypt from the Mokattam Formation.
Computed tomography scans revealed many anatomical differences between Herugavialis and other Egyptian crocodilians of its time, such as Eogavialis africanum and Paratomistoma courti.
Taxonomists classify Herugavialis as a member of the superfamily Gavialoidea.
The fossil record places Herugavialis in the Eocene epoch, specifically the Lutetian stage.
Some records alternatively list the age as the Middle Miocene.
Scientists debate whether a drop in Mediterranean gavialoid diversity resulted from habitat loss caused by global cooling and falling sea levels.
Another question concerns whether Miocene warming allowed diversity to recover before the Late Miocene extinction triggered by the Messinian Salinity Crisis.
